data.text: React Hook Form minimizes re-renders by using uncontrolled components and ref-based registration.

data.title: React Hook Form

data.text: React Hook Form keeps input values in refs rather than component state, so typing does not rerender the whole form. You spread `register` onto an input to connect it, and read values through `handleSubmit` instead of tracking each field. This is why it stays fast on large forms.

data.title: A typed form with validation

data.text: Instead of hand-writing each rule in `register`, a resolver validates the whole form against one schema, so the form and the API share the same source of truth. `zodResolver` connects Zod to the form, and `mode` controls when validation runs — on submit, on blur, or on change.

data.title: Zod resolver in one place
Interview angle: controlled vs uncontrolled
data.text: A controlled input stores every keystroke in React state, which rerenders on each change; an uncontrolled input lets the DOM hold the value and reads it on submit or through a ref. React Hook Form trades a little re-render-level reactivity for far better performance on big forms. Name that trade-off — it is the whole reason the library exists.

terms.definition: Form elements managed by DOM refs.
